newsitem.title: GERMANY: Swissair eyes Frankfurt-Zurich air cargo rail link.
newsitem.headline: Swissair eyes Frankfurt-Zurich air cargo rail link.

text.p: Swissair said it hopes to switch much of its ex-Germany air cargo tonnage from road trucking services to rail transport next year.

Ulf Steinmann, Swissair cargo manager Germany, told Reuters in an interview the airline is discussing with Deutsche Bahn AG (DB) launching a Frankfurt airport-Zurich rail feeder service in autumn 1997.

Air cargo containers would be carried overnight in a newly-designed DB Cargo Sprinter train from Frankfurt airport's Cargo City South complex railhead instead of being transported across the Alps by truck, he said.
Containers would be loaded from aircraft on to the train at a terminal planned by Swissair air cargo handling partner Georg Reischel Luftfracht GmbH next to the Cargo City South rail link, he added.
Steinmann said: "If it happens, we would bring our entire freight which is transported by road on to the railway."
This would amount to a monthly volume of about 1,200 tonnes of high-value air cargo exports, he said.
The Frankfurt-Zurich air cargo shuttle would then carry 80-90 percent Swissair freight generated from Frankfurt and northern German airports, he said.
"We estimate we would have a load factor depending on the weekday of 60-100 percent," he added.
Steinmann said he expected Lufthansa Cargo AG also to be involved in the venture.
Swissair is now waiting for a clear offer from DB as to how the service can operate and at what price, he added.
"The pre-condition is that DB makes an attractive offer which can compete with the road price.
"If the price is about the same as for road transport, then we will switch. We do not expect a dumping price from DB but we want cost transparency," he said.
Steinmann declined to disclose what rates Swissair pays for trucking services at present but noted the market is very competitive.
The train would depart Frankfurt airport between midnight and 0100 local time arriving in Zurich between 0600 and 0700, making the return journey by day.
A logical expansion of the service would be to operate a night departure from Zurich with a day return from Frankfurt airport, he added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
